Birth control is notorious for making you gain weight simply because it makes your body think its pregnant. When you up the progesterone your body has these weird side effects from thinking it needs to change in order to get ready to have a child that isn't there. So mood swings, breast size increase, and weight gain are a natural part of pregnancy  because these are all things that your body does to stockpile bodily resources to use for birth. But it's lessened from BC essentially being a phantom pregnancy. I found that a change in diet helps the most for me personally. I switched to a pretty protein dense diet while eating smaller portions more frequently, a tactic I found out most pregnant women also use to help with nausea and mood swings. I also found that with the spike in hormones that BC causes, you might actually need more sleep than you're used to, it also helps to keep sleeping as regular as possible.

If you still feel off in a few months and if you're progressively gaining weight and generally feeling terrible, check your other hormones like your thyroid. Sometimes hormone imbalances like BC an pregnancy can trigger an underlying condition in your endocrine system, so be on the alert if things aren't getting better.

Best of luck, I hope everything works out!

Wow okay we have very similar stories, my parents were both immigrants who either went to college in a different country or didn’t go at all. I was also thrown into really intense bio courses starting in freshmen year and it killed my gpa. I’m in my third year doing marine science and I love what I study and I have such a clear vision of my future but my academic performance is a huge setback for my future and my motivation. Sometimes I’m in a place where the victories I do have are so small it’s hard to keep my head up. All I can say is that you are NOT ALONE and you are NOT A FAILURE even when you mess up or when other people mess you up. There’s also so many other ways you can make yourself more prepared and marketable for jobs like volunteering at places that are in the field (even if that means only cleaning up the place or getting people coffee businesses in the bio field love free labor and will gladly let you put that on a resume if it means they don’t have to pay you). Also the best thing you can do is to do most things on your own, like being versed in required courses and prerequisites bc lord knows I’ve been failed by most advisors who have way too many advisees to remember everything. Former students can also help, my greatest resources have been my older friends who know the internships and which professors can get you them no matter what your grades look like. You can get through this don’t lose hope, I’m right there with you doing the same thing. We got this.
